## 1.5 million euros: the municipal commitment to biodiversity

The breakdown of the investment reveals a strategy that goes far beyond simple maintenance. Of the more than 1.5 million euros executed since 2021, a substantial portion has been allocated to the restoration of the water bodies, the element that defines the very essence of the wetland. La Charca de Suárez depends on a delicate water balance, conditioned by contributions from the aquifer and by the network of irrigation channels that historically drained the fertile plain. Recovering the flooding capacity of the different lagoons that make up the space has required waterproofing works, sediment cleaning, and the adaptation of sluice gates. Without permanent water, the birdlife that today finds refuge in this corner of the Granada coast would simply disappear.

The Motril City Council has not faced this task alone. The financing has been supported by European funds and the Junta de Andalucía, channeled through wetland conservation and sustainable rural development programs. This inter-administrative collaboration has made it possible to undertake actions that would otherwise have been unaffordable for the municipal treasury. The restoration of the water bodies has also included the installation of recirculation systems that optimize the use of a resource as scarce as fresh water on the Mediterranean coast. Every cubic meter lost to evaporation or filtration represents a threat to the biodiversity that depends on this enclave.

The second major item of investment has gone to the construction and equipping of the interpretation center. This building, recently inaugurated, is not a simple tourist information point. It has been conceived as the gateway to an ecosystem that many visitors do not know how to read without help. The center houses explanatory panels about the species that inhabit the pond, models that reproduce the hydrological functioning of the wetland, and an audiovisual room where documentaries filmed in the space itself are shown. The municipal commitment to environmental education materializes in a facility that aspires to receive schoolchildren from across the province and to become a reference for family tourism.

The improvement of the trails has been another of the actions financed under this budget item. The paths surrounding the different lagoons were in an irregular state, with sections that flooded in winter and others that were not very accessible for people with reduced mobility. The intervention has made it possible to consolidate the surface, install wooden walkways at the most sensitive points, and equip bird observatories with informational panels. These infrastructures, apparently modest, are decisive for managing the flow of visitors and preventing human traffic from degrading nesting areas. An urban wetland like La Charca de Suárez needs to reconcile public use with strict conservation, and well-designed trails are the most effective tool to achieve this.

The hiring of specialized personnel has consumed another significant part of the budget. For years, La Charca de Suárez depended on the volunteer work of environmental groups and the goodwill of some municipal technicians. The recent investment has made it possible to bring in environmental educators, ornithological guides, and maintenance staff with specific training in wetland management. This team is responsible for guided visits, monitoring bird populations, and daily conservation tasks. The professionalization of the service has raised the quality of the visitor experience and has provided the space with a management capacity that did not previously exist.

The strategic plan framing this investment has a declared objective: to position La Charca de Suárez as a reference for ornithological tourism in Andalusia. The autonomous community has top-tier enclaves such as Doñana or the Fuente de Piedra lagoon, but the Granada coast until now lacked an accessible and well-managed wetland that could compete in that segment. Birdwatching tourism moves thousands of travelers each year with a medium-high spending profile and extended stays. Motril aspires to capture a part of that flow, offering a natural space of great ecological value a short distance from the beach and the hotel offering of the Costa Tropical.

The municipal investment has not been limited to public works. A portion of the funds has been allocated to outreach campaigns and the publication of educational materials that explain the value of the wetland. Scientific studies on the evolution of waterbird populations and water quality have also been funded. These works, carried out in collaboration with Andalusian universities, provide objective data that support management decisions. La Charca de Suárez has become a small open-air laboratory where ecological restoration techniques are tested that could be applied to other coastal wetlands in the Mediterranean.

The return on this investment is not measured only in economic terms. The recovery of La Charca de Suárez has returned to Motril a natural space that for decades was condemned to oblivion. Residents have rediscovered a place that forms part of their territorial identity, a landscape of water and reeds that contrasts with the tourist image of sun and beach associated with the Costa Tropical. The municipal commitment to biodiversity has transformed an environmental liability into a social, educational, and tourist asset. The 1.5 million euros invested represent, in this sense, a political decision that transcends the electoral cycle and commits future corporations to the conservation of this unique enclave on the Andalusian coast.
